hints: Write the liquid volume as base area multiplied by depth: V = Ah.
Use density to express the mass of this volume, then use W = mg before substituting into p = F / A.
walkthrough: The liquid above the base has volume V = Ah, so from ρ = m / V, its mass is m = ρAh.
Its weight is W = mg = ρAhg, and this is the force on the base.
Using p = F / A gives p = ρAhg / A = ρgh, which is the hydrostatic-pressure relation for this depth.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses ρ = m / V with V = Ah, or equivalently writes ρ = m / Ah.
Uses p = F / A or p = W / A for the pressure on the base.
Uses W = mg and the preceding definitions to obtain p = ρgh by appropriate cancellation of A.

hints: The expression from part (a) accounts only for the pressure produced by the liquid column.
Consider the pressure exerted on the liquid surface by the air.
walkthrough: The quantity ρgh is the pressure contribution from the liquid column.
Air above the liquid also exerts atmospheric pressure, which is transmitted to the base.
Therefore ρgh alone is not the total pressure on the base.

ai_rubric.observable: States that atmospheric or air pressure also contributes to the total pressure on the base.

hints: Use two well-separated points on the graph, so the atmospheric-pressure contribution cancels when you find the pressure difference.
Convert the 8.0 cm depth difference to metres before using Δp = ρgΔh.
walkthrough: From the graph, pressure increases from 9.60 × 10⁴ Pa at 0 cm to 9.66 × 10⁴ Pa at 8.0 cm, so Δp = 600 Pa.
The depth difference is Δh = 8.0 cm = 8.0 × 10⁻² m.
Using Δp = ρgΔh gives ρ = 600 / (9.81 × 8.0 × 10⁻²) = 765 kg m⁻³.
This is within the accepted range, so the density is about 760–770 kg m⁻³.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the graph pressure difference of 600 Pa and depth difference of 8.0 × 10⁻² m in Δp = ρgΔh.
Obtains a density in the accepted range 760–770 kg m⁻³.

hints: When the cylinder is fully immersed, calculate the volume of liquid displaced from its cross-sectional area and length.
The extra upward upthrust reduces the tension needed to keep the cylinder stationary.
Alternatively, obtain the pressure difference over the cylinder length from Fig. 4.2 and multiply it by the cross-sectional area.
walkthrough: With its top at the liquid surface, the cylinder is fully immersed, so the displaced volume is V = 3.7 × 10⁻⁴ × 4.0 × 10⁻² m³.
The upthrust is F = ρgV = 765 × 9.81 × 3.7 × 10⁻⁴ × 4.0 × 10⁻² = 0.11 N (approximately).
Because the cylinder remains stationary, the additional upward upthrust reduces the wire tension: T = 0.53 − 0.11 = 0.42 N.
Equivalent route: the graph gives a 300 Pa pressure difference over 4.0 cm, so F = ΔpA = 300 × 3.7 × 10⁻⁴ = 0.11 N, leading to the same tension.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates an upthrust of about 0.11 N using F = ρgV, or equivalently uses the 300 Pa pressure difference and F = ΔpA.
Subtracts the 0.11 N upthrust from 0.53 N to obtain a new tension of 0.42 N.
